title: Crystal Palace’s Eddie Nketiah out for rest of season with hamstring injury
content:
Crystal Palace manager Oliver Glasner says that Eddie Nketiah will be sidelined for the rest of the season with his fourth hamstring injury of the campaign.

The 26-year-old has not featured for the south London side since their 1-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur on December 28.

In February, Glasner said Nketiah was expected to return to the pitch in April but the Austrian said before Palace’s 3-0 Conference League win against Fiorentina that the former Arsenal striker had “injured his hamstring again” in training and would not be in the squad. After Thursday’s quarter-final, Glasner gave a further update on Nketiah’s injury.

“For Eddie, unfortunately, it’s the end to the season,” Glanser said. “This (news) came yesterday evening (Wednesday). The doctor called me at nine in the evening when I was watching the Champions League games, so it’s really brand new.

“I will speak to him tomorrow (Friday) and then we’ll decide what’s best because, like Cheick Doucoure, it is (about) getting stable. Now, the deadline is not Newcastle or Florence, it should be when the new pre-season starts, that he’s in the best shape and can train for the full preseason, definitely with a new manager because that’s what he deserves and needs: constant training and games to get back to match fitness and we will support him.”

Nketiah has made only 19 appearances in all competitions for Palace this season, registering four goals and one assist. The attacker has missed 30 matches due to injury in the 2025-26 campaign, due to four separate hamstring problems.

Nketiah is under contract with Palace until 2029, having signed a five-year deal in 2024 following his transfer from Arsenal. Last season, he played in 37 matches — scoring seven goals and providing three assists — including a substitute appearance in their historic FA Cup final win against Manchester City.

Glasner also provided fitness updates for Evann Guessand and Jean-Philippe Mateta ahead of Palace’s Premier League home match against Newcastle United on Sunday. Guessand was taken off in the 66th minute while Mateta, who scored a first-half penalty, came off in the 84th minute.

“We have to assess Evann’s knee. He got a hit, let’s see — he could walk,” Glasner said. “We have to see how JP’s knee reacts but Jorgen Strand Larsen and Uche (will) come back, we’ll have more attacking options and that’s good.”

Glasner confirmed that Doucoure was also not available, having only returned for the Under-21s last month from a 14-month meniscus knee injury lay-off.
